page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 processor architecture. The configuration supplies 64 dedicated virtual CPUs and 248.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced density of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This hardware profile features no graphics processing units, directing all system power entirely toward standard central processing operations.

Storage functionality on the c4d-standard-64 is not bundled locally, as local disk capacity is listed as none. Operating systems and working data sets must rely on external network-attached block storage. The instance configuration also provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced ratio of compute to memory minimizes resource idling across multi-threaded applications requiring neither extreme memory density nor local disk caching.

With 64 dedicated cores and a 248.0 GB memory footprint, the c4d-standard-64 is suited for mid-sized to large-scale enterprise services. Workload fits include container orchestration nodes, continuous integration and deployment builders, backend application servers, and web serving clusters operating alongside remote storage backends.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-64 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine designed for horizontally and vertically scaling workloads. It provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs and 248.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is provisioned without local disk storage, necessitating external block storage solutions for data persistence and operating system installations. Furthermore, it operates without GPU acceleration and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dedicated vCPU model ensures predictable multi-core performance across high-concurrency tasks without host CPU oversubscription. Given its symmetric allocation of compute and memory resources, this server type delivers balanced resource efficiency for container clusters, CI/CD build environments, enterprise application servers, and distributed backends that run against network-attached storage.
